Majority vote across noisy variants beats single-variant consensus that matches the receipt structure."},{"id":"rc2","summary":"Highest-priority tier wins even on a pure fallback match","detail":"When a higher-priority keyword (e.g. GRAND TOTAL) exists but its own line has no number, the split-line fallback can land on a payment/change/cash-received line. Because that tier outranks everything, a correct tier-3 TOTAL value is suppressed by a bad tier-0 fallback."},{"id":"rc3","summary":"'Last candidate wins' picks the wrong TOTAL when a 'Rounding' line follows","detail":"For receipts whose layout is Total(Inclusive) / Rounding Adj / TOTAL:, picking the LAST TOTAL-keyword line is correct, but picking the first/earlier one (pre-rounding) yields the wrong amount by a few cents. The current ordering logic plus exclusion of 'Rounding Adj' can cause the final-total line to be missed when OCR mangles it."},{"id":"rc4","summary":"Missing/unparseable fields written as empty string instead of real null","detail":"The Excel writer emitted \"\" for 078.total_amount instead of Python None, so the cell is a non-empty string and fails exact-equality grading against an expected null."},{"id":"rc5","summary":"Date extraction returns first regex match without disambiguating DD/MM vs MM/DD or multiple dates on the receipt","detail":"When a receipt contains more than one date-like token (invoice print date, transaction date, loyalty date), the earliest-match-wins strategy can select a non-primary date, and DD/MM/YYYY vs MM/DD/YYYY ambiguity is resolved only by pattern order."}],"skill_defects":[{"skill":"image-ocr","defect":"The structured-field extraction section documents keyword priority, exclusions and a two-line fallback, but does not require (a) cross-line value corroboration when voting across OCR variants, (b) restricting the two-line fallback so it cannot land on payment/cash/visa/change lines, or (c) preferring the LAST occurrence of a TOTAL keyword when multiple appear (pre-rounding vs after-rounding)."},{"skill":"image-ocr","defect":"Exclusion list does not cover common non-total lines that carry 'RM' or 'TOTAL'-adjacent wording: 'Visa', result."},{"skill":"image-ocr","defect":"Date extraction guidance returns the first match without a tie-break that prefers the date nearest an invoice/receipt/transaction keyword, and does not discuss before to_excel, nor a post-write verification that empty-expected cells actually read back as NaN/None (not empty string)."},{"skill":"xlsx","defect":"The verification snippet checks column names, for strict-schema outputs the entire DataFrame should be coerced to object dtype BEFORE assigning None, otherwise pandas may upcast None to NaN in a numeric column and the grader sees a different cell next non-empty line ONLY if that line is not an exclusion line AND does not match a payment-method pattern (VISA|MASTERCARD|MASTER|AMEX|DEBIT|CREDIT|CARD|CASH|E-?WALLET|TNG|GRABPAY|POINTS|LOYALTY|RM\\s*PAID|PAID|BALANCE). If the keyword line has digits but they fail to parse as a valid decimal, do NOT fall through."},{"target":"image-ocr","change":"Expand EXCLUSIONS to include: 'VISA', 'MASTERCARD', 'AMEX', 'DEBIT', 'CREDIT CARD', 'CASH RECEIVED', 'CASH PAYMENT', 'CASH TENDER', 'PAID', 'BALANCE', 'POINTS', 'TOTAL GROSS', 'TOTAL SALES', 'TOTAL (EXCLUDING', 'TOTAL EXCL', 'AMT EXCL', 'EXCL. GST', 'EXCLUSIVE', 'AVERAGE'. Document that exclusion matching is substring/regex-based and case-insensitive and is checked BEFORE priority-tier matching."},{"target":"image-ocr","change":"Specify a 'prefer last-in-reading-order' rule when multiple candidates match the same priority tier, with the explicit note that receipts often print pre-rounding 'Total Incl. of GST' before 'Rounding Adj' before the final 'TOTAL' line, and the final one is authoritative."},{"target":"image-ocr","change":"Document a cross-variant voting policy for structured fields: (1) for each OCR variant, collect ALL (tier, value) candidates, not just the best; (2) pick the lowest tier index that has any candidate; (3) within that tier, score each value by variant-count + number of same-receipt lines (in any variant) whose last number equals that value (subtotal/payment corroboration); (4) break remaining ties by last-in-reading-order. State that single-variant majority voting without corroboration is insufficient."},{"target":"image-ocr","change":"Add a date-selection heuristic: prefer the date token on a line containing 'date', 'invoice', 'receipt', 'trans', 'tax invoice', or 'bill'; if no such line exists, prefer the earliest date in the top half of the receipt; default DD/MM/YYYY interpretation for ambiguous two-digit day/month when day>12 is possible elsewhere in the file, and document this assumption."},{"target":"image-ocr","change":"Add an explicit null-contract line: 'extract_total' and 'extract_date' must return Python None (not '', 'None', 0, NaN, or 'null') when extraction fails; callers must preserve None through to the output writer."},{"target":"xlsx","change":"In the Strict-Schema section, add a mandatory 'null sanitization' step immediately before to_excel: iterate the rows/DataFrame and replace '', 'None', 'none', 'NaN', 'nan', float('nan'), and pandas.NA with Python None, after coercing the affected columns to object dtype."},{"target":"xlsx","change":"Extend the post-write verification snippet to assert, for every non-null total_amount: value matches regex ^\\d+\\.\\d{2}$ (no commas, no currency, no whitespace, exactly two decimals); and for every date: value matches ^\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}$. Also assert that cells intended to be null read back as NaN/None, not as the strings '' or 'nan'."},{"target":"xlsx","change":"Add a short note: when building the DataFrame from a list of dicts that may contain None, set dtype='object' on string-typed columns BEFORE writing, so pandas does not coerce None to NaN in a way that round-trips as the string 'nan' through to_excel/read_excel."},{"target":"openai-vision","change":"Add a 'Disambiguation Fallback' subsection: when a tesseract-based pipeline yields conflicting candidate values for a structured field (e.g., two different totals from different OCR variants, or two plausible dates), optionally call gpt-4o-mini with detail='high' on that single image and ask for ONLY the final total / receipt date as strict JSON; use the returned value to break the tie. Note that this is a tie-breaker, not a primary extractor, to control cost."},{"target":"image-ocr","change":"Document a 'summary band' heuristic for receipts: once a line matches a payment-method or 'change'/'balance' keyword, treat all following lines as out-of-scope for total extraction; this prevents the two-line fallback from drifting into the post-total area."},{"target":"image-ocr","change":"Add a 'sanity check' step for the chosen total: if the extracted value differs by >15% from the sum of parsed line-item amounts (when those can be read), log a warning and prefer a lower-tier candidate that is within tolerance; this directly addresses OCR digit-confusion cases like 102 vs 702."}],"confidence":"medium"}
